items.question: Under which article is the Advocate General of State appointed?
items.explanation: Advocate General of State is appointed under Article 165.

items.subject: Polity
items.chapter: Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
items.question: Who shall make rules for more convenient transaction of the business of Government of India and allocate responsibilities among Ministers according to Article 77(3)?
items.explanation: The President shall make rules for convenient transaction of government business under Article 77(3).

items.subject: Polity
items.chapter: Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
items.question: Article 78(a) requires the Prime Minister to communicate to the President all decisions of the Council of Ministers relating to:
options: administration of the Union and proposals for legislation
items.correctAnswer: administration of the Union and proposals for legislation
items.explanation: Article 78(a) requires communicating decisions relating to administration of the Union and proposals for legislation.
items.optionC: administration of the Union and proposals for legislation

items.subject: Polity
items.chapter: Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
items.question: Under Article 78(b), who can call for information relating to the administration of the Union and proposals for legislation?
items.explanation: Article 78(b) allows the President to call for such information regarding administration and legislation.

items.subject: Polity
items.chapter: Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
items.question: Article 78(c) allows the President to require the submission of a matter for the consideration of the Council of Ministers if:
options: a decision has been taken by a Minister but not considered by the Council
items.correctAnswer: a decision has been taken by a Minister but not considered by the Council
items.explanation: Article 78(c) applies if a decision was taken by a Minister but not considered by the Council.
items.optionB: a decision has been taken by a Minister but not considered by the Council

items.subject: Polity
items.chapter: Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
items.question: Who stated: 'Collective responsibility can be achieved only through the instrumentality of the Prime Minister'?
items.explanation: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar made this comment on the post of the PM.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Which of the following states has 16 seats in the Rajya Sabha according to the table?
items.explanation: Both West Bengal and Bihar have 16 seats in the Rajya Sabha.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Which article deals with the composition of the House of the People (Lok Sabha)?
items.explanation: Article 81 details the composition of the House of the People.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Through which Constitutional Amendment Act was the provision for nominating Anglo-Indians removed?
items.explanation: The Anglo-Indian nomination provision was removed through the 104th CAA, 2019.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: What does the green color inside the Lok Sabha represent, according to the notes?
options: Agricultural land and people elected from grassroots level
Peace and prosperity of the nation
Royalty and sacrifices of freedom fighters
items.correctAnswer: Agricultural land and people elected from grassroots level
items.explanation: Green color represents agricultural land and people elected from grassroots level.
items.optionA: Agricultural land and people elected from grassroots level
items.optionB: Peace and prosperity of the nation
items.optionC: Royalty and sacrifices of freedom fighters

items.subject: Polity
items.question: What does the red color inside the Rajya Sabha represent?
options: Royalty and sacrifices done by freedom fighters and blood shed
items.correctAnswer: Royalty and sacrifices done by freedom fighters and blood shed
items.explanation: Red color represents royalty and symbolises sacrifices done by freedom fighters.
items.optionD: Royalty and sacrifices done by freedom fighters and blood shed

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Which Article of the Constitution provides for readjustment after each census?
items.explanation: Article 82 provides for Readjustment after Each Census.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: How often is a Delimitation Commission established to divide constituencies based on population?
items.explanation: A Delimitation Commission is established after every census (in 10 years).

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Which of the following was the year of the 3rd Delimitation Act mentioned in the notes?
items.explanation: The 3rd Delimitation Act year listed is 1972.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Under which Constitutional Amendment Act were seats fixed based on the 1971 Census until 2000?
items.explanation: 42nd CA (1976) fixed seats based on the 1971 census until 2000.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Up to which year was the freeze on the Delimitation Commission extended by the 84th CA (2001)?
items.explanation: The 84th CA extended the freeze on Delimitation till 2026.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Which articles of the Indian Constitution deal with Parliament under Part V?
items.explanation: Part V Parliament covers Article 79 to 122 as per the notes.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: What is the normal tenure of the Lok Sabha?
items.explanation: The tenure of Lok Sabha is 5 years.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: What is the maximum allowed gap between two sessions of Parliament?
items.explanation: The maximum gap between sessions cannot exceed 6 months.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: What fraction of members of the Rajya Sabha retire every two years?
items.explanation: 1/3rd members of Rajya Sabha retire every 2 years.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: What is the term of office for an individual member of the Rajya Sabha?
items.explanation: The term of members of RS is 6 years.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Which of the following houses is a permanent body and not subject to dissolution?
items.explanation: Rajya Sabha is a permanent body; not subject to dissolution.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: How many Lok Sabha seats are allotted to Bihar according to the table on page 65?
items.explanation: Bihar has 40 Lok Sabha seats listed in the table.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: What is the minimum required age to become a member of the Rajya Sabha?
items.explanation: Article 84 states the minimum required age is 30 years for Rajya Sabha.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Which article deals with the Sessions of Parliament, Prorogation, and Dissolution?
items.explanation: Article 85 covers sessions, prorogation, and dissolution of Parliament on the Council of Ministers' advice.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: During which months does the Budget Session of Parliament typically take place?
items.explanation: The Budget Session runs from February to April.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: How many members' support is needed to admit an adjournment motion in Parliament?
items.explanation: An adjournment motion needs the support of 50 members to be admitted.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: According to Article 79, the Parliament of India consists of which of the following?
options: Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, and Prime Minister
items.explanation: Article 79 states that Parliament consists of the President plus Two Houses.
items.optionD: Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, and Prime Minister

items.subject: Polity
items.question: What is the duration of a Short Notice question's advance notice requirement?
items.explanation: Short Notice questions require 10 days prior notice to be given.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: At what time does the Question Hour take place during a routine Parliamentary session?
items.explanation: Question Hour is scheduled from 11 AM to 12 PM.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Under which article does the President have the right to address and send messages to Houses?
items.explanation: Article 86 grants the President the right to address either House or both houses jointly.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: What follows the special address by the President under Article 87?
items.explanation: A Motion of Thanks follows the special address by the President.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Who serves as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
items.explanation: The Vice President of India acts as the ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: How is the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha removed from office?
items.explanation: Removal requires an Effective majority of the total membership of the Rajya Sabha.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Who was the first woman to be appointed to the Rajya Sabha panel of Vice-Chairpersons?
items.explanation: P.T. Usha is the first woman appointed to the RS panel of Vice-Chairpersons.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Who was the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
items.explanation: Ganesh Vasudev Mavalankar was the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Since what year has no Deputy Speaker been appointed in the Lok Sabha according to the notes?
items.explanation: No Deputy Speaker has been appointed since 2019.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Who fixes the date of election for the Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
items.explanation: The date of election of the Speaker is fixed by the President.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: In which year was the Hindi name 'Lok Sabha' adopted for the House of the People?
items.explanation: The Hindi name for Lok Sabha was adopted in 1954.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Who administers the oath or affirmation to every member of either House of Parliament?
options: The President or a person appointed by him
items.correctAnswer: The President or a person appointed by him
items.explanation: Oath is administered by the President or a person appointed by him.
items.optionA: The President or a person appointed by him

items.subject: Polity
items.question: From which date to which date did Bhartruhari Mahtab serve as Protem Speaker after 2024 elections?
items.explanation: He served as Protem Speaker from 24th June 2024 to 26th June 2024.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: What fraction of the total strength of the House constitutes the quorum under Article 100(3)?
items.explanation: Quorum requires a minimum of 1/10th of the total strength of the House.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Under Article 101(4), a house may declare a seat vacant if a member is absent without permission for how many days?
items.explanation: Absence without permission for a period of 60 days allows the house to declare the seat vacant.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: According to the RPA 1951 note, imprisonment for more than how many years leads to disqualification?
items.explanation: Jail for more than two years leads to disqualification under RPA 1951.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Within how many months from nomination can a nominated member join a political party without disqualification?
items.explanation: Nominated members can join a political party after 6 months from the date of nomination.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Which constitutional amendment introduced an exception for merger concerning two-third members under the 10th Schedule?
items.explanation: The 91st CA, 2003 added the merger exception when 2/3rd members leave and join another party.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: In which case was it established that the judiciary can review the final decision of the Speaker regarding disqualification under defection?
items.explanation: Kihoto Holohan vs Zachilhu Case ruled that the judiciary can review the Speaker's final decision.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: What is the duration of the Zero Hour during a Parliamentary session?
items.explanation: Zero Hour takes place from 12-1 PM where the agenda of the day is decided.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Which motion requires no reason to be stated and can be moved against the entire council of ministers only?
items.explanation: No-Confidence Motion requires no reason and is moved against the entire council only.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: When was the first sitting of the Lok Sabha held?
items.explanation: The first sitting of Lok Sabha took place on 13 May 1952.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: What happens if a No-Confidence Motion is passed in the Lok Sabha?
items.explanation: If the No-Confidence Motion is passed, resignation of the council of ministers is mandatory.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: What is the total maximum number of members in the Rajya Sabha as given in the notes?
items.explanation: The total member strength of Rajya Sabha is 250.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: How many members are nominated by the President to the Rajya Sabha from specified fields?
items.explanation: 12 members are nominated by the President to the Rajya Sabha.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: From which country was the election of Rajya Sabha members borrowed into the Indian Constitution?
items.explanation: Election of RS members was borrowed from South Africa.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: From which country was the nomination of members to the Rajya Sabha taken?
items.explanation: Nomination of RS members is taken from Ireland.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: How many seats are represented for Uttar Pradesh in the Rajya Sabha?
items.explanation: Uttar Pradesh has 31 seats in the Rajya Sabha.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Who presides over the Joint Sitting of both Houses according to Article 108(2)?
items.explanation: Article 108(2) states the Speaker of Lok Sabha presides over the Joint Sitting.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Can the Chairman of Rajya Sabha preside over a Joint Sitting?
options: No, as he is not the member of either house
Yes, in absence of Lok Sabha Speaker
items.correctAnswer: No, as he is not the member of either house
items.explanation: Chairman cannot preside the Joint sitting as he is not the member of either house.
items.optionB: No, as he is not the member of either house
items.optionC: Yes, in absence of Lok Sabha Speaker

items.subject: Polity
items.question: How many times have joint sittings happened in India according to the notes?
items.explanation: Joint Sittings has happened 3 times in India's legislative history.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Which of the following bills had a joint sitting?
items.explanation: Dowry Prohibition Bill, 1960 is listed as one of the bills with joint sittings.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Which bills have no joint sitting allowed as an exception?
options: Public Member Bill and Private Bill
Money Bill and Constitutional Amendment Bill
items.correctAnswer: Money Bill and Constitutional Amendment Bill
items.explanation: Money Bill and Constitutional Amendment Bill have no joint sitting allowed.
items.optionA: Public Member Bill and Private Bill
items.optionC: Money Bill and Constitutional Amendment Bill

items.subject: Polity
items.question: According to Article 109(1), a Money Bill can only be introduced in Lok Sabha on whose recommendation?
items.explanation: A Money Bill can only be introduced in Lok Sabha on the recommendation of the President.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Within how many days must Rajya Sabha return or respond to a Money Bill?
items.explanation: Rajya Sabha must give its response to a Money Bill within 14 days.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Who certifies whether a Bill is a Money Bill?
items.explanation: The Speaker of Lok Sabha certifies whether a Bill is a Money Bill.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Is judicial review allowed on the Speaker's decision regarding a Money Bill?
items.explanation: The Speaker's decision is final and normally cannot be challenged, however, Judicial review is allowed.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Under which Article is the definition of a Money Bill given?
items.explanation: Article 110 covers the definition of a Money Bill.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Which Article states that a Bill can originate in either House (LS or RS) except the Money bill?
items.explanation: Article 107(1) states a Bill can originate in either House except the Money bill.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: What is the nature of Veto Powers of the President in India?
items.explanation: Veto Powers of President is Negative in Nature.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: In which veto power does the President return the Bill for reconsideration?
items.explanation: President returns the Bill for reconsideration under Suspensiveness Veto.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Suspensive veto is not available in case of which bill?
items.explanation: Suspensive veto is not available in case of Money bill.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Who first used the Pocket Veto for the Indian Post Office (amendment) bill 1986?
items.explanation: Pocket veto was first used by Gyani Zail Singh for Indian Post Office bill 1986.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Can any Veto be used in the case of a Constitutional Bill (Article 368)?
options: Yes, Pocket Veto can be used
No Veto can be used in case of a Constitutional Bill
Only Absolute Veto can be used
Yes, Suspensive Veto can be used
items.correctAnswer: No Veto can be used in case of a Constitutional Bill
items.explanation: No Veto can be used in case of a Constitutional Bill 24th CA (Article 368).
items.optionA: Yes, Pocket Veto can be used
items.optionB: No Veto can be used in case of a Constitutional Bill
items.optionC: Only Absolute Veto can be used
items.optionD: Yes, Suspensive Veto can be used

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Why is the Pocket of Indian President deeper than the USA's president?
options: Because no time limit is mentioned in constitution for Indian president
items.correctAnswer: Because no time limit is mentioned in constitution for Indian president
items.explanation: Pocket of Indian President is deeper because no time limit is mentioned in constitution.
items.optionA: Because no time limit is mentioned in constitution for Indian president

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Which article deals with the Annual Financial Statement (Budget)?
items.explanation: Article 112 covers the Annual Financial Statement, though the term budget is not in the Constitution.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Which House has the exclusive right to vote on Demands for Grants?
items.explanation: Only Lok Sabha has the right to vote on Demands for Grants.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: What is the purpose of a Policy Cut motion?
options: Reduce the amount to Rs. 1 to criticize government policy
Reduce a specified amount to suggest savings
items.correctAnswer: Reduce the amount to Rs. 1 to criticize government policy
items.explanation: Policy Cut reduces the amount to Rs. 1 to criticize government policy.
items.optionA: Reduce the amount to Rs. 1 to criticize government policy
items.optionB: Reduce a specified amount to suggest savings

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Which grant acts like a blank cheque given to the Executive by Lok Sabha?
items.explanation: Votes on Credit act like a blank cheque given to the Executive by the Lok Sabha.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: According to Article 107(3), what happens to a Bill pending in Parliament due to adjournment or prorogation?
options: It is referred to a joint sitting
items.explanation: Article 107(3) states a Bill pending in Parliament does not lapse due to adjournment or prorogation.
items.optionD: It is referred to a joint sitting

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Under which Article is the Consolidated Fund of India established?
items.explanation: Consolidated Fund of India is established under Article 266 (1).

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Who manages the Public Account of India?
items.explanation: Public Account of India is managed by the Executive.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: The Contingency Fund of India is run by the President and whom?
items.explanation: Contingency Fund of India is run by the President and Finance Secretary.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: An ordinance issued by the President ceases to operate after how many weeks from reassembly unless approved?
items.explanation: An ordinance ceases to operate after 6 weeks from reassembly unless approved.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Which Article grants the President the power to promulgate ordinances during recess?
items.explanation: Article 123 gives the President the power to promulgate ordinances during recess.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: No discussions shall take place in Parliament regarding the conduct of any judge of which courts?
options: Supreme Court or a High Court
items.correctAnswer: Supreme Court or a High Court
items.explanation: No discussions shall take place regarding the conduct of any judge of the Supreme Court or a High Court.
items.optionC: Supreme Court or a High Court

items.subject: Polity
items.question: What is the maximum life of an ordinance if Parliament takes no action and the maximum gap between sessions applies?
items.explanation: Max life is 6 months and 6 weeks if Parliament takes no action.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Which article allows Rajya Sabha to authorize Parliament to create a new All India Service?
items.explanation: Article 312 allows Rajya Sabha to authorize Parliament to create a new All India Service.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: When was the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) established?
items.explanation: Public Accounts Committee was established in 1921 through GOI Act 1919.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: What is the total number of members in the Public Accounts Committee?
items.explanation: Total members in PAC are 22, with 15 from Lok Sabha and 7 from Rajya Sabha.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Under Article 107(4), what happens to a Bill pending in Lok Sabha and not passed at the time of its dissolution?
options: It goes to Rajya Sabha automatically
It is passed by simple majority
items.explanation: Article 107(4) states a Bill pending in Lok Sabha and not passed at dissolution lapses.
items.optionB: It goes to Rajya Sabha automatically
items.optionD: It is passed by simple majority

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Who acts as the guide and philosopher to the Public Accounts Committee?
items.explanation: CAG acts as the guide and philosopher to the Public Accounts Committee.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: On whose recommendation was the Estimates Committee re-established post-independence in 1950?
items.explanation: Estimates Committee was re-established on recommendation of John Mathai Committee in 1950.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: How many total members are in the Estimates Committee?
items.explanation: Estimates Committee has 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: When was the Committee on Public Undertakings established?
items.explanation: Committee on Public Undertakings was established in 1964 on recommendation of Krishna Menon Committee.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: What is the total member strength of the Committee on Public Undertakings?
items.explanation: Committee on Public Undertakings has 22 members (15 from LS + 7 from RS).

items.subject: Polity
items.question: What is the term of members in Financial Committees?
items.explanation: The term of members in financial committees is 1 year.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Can a Minister be a member of any Financial Committee?
options: No Minister can be a member
items.correctAnswer: No Minister can be a member
items.explanation: No Minister can be a member of the financial committees (only private member).
items.optionD: No Minister can be a member

items.subject: Polity
items.question: What is the total number of Departmental Standing Committees?
items.explanation: There are a total of 24 Departmental Standing Committees.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: What is the total strength of members in each Departmental Standing Committee?
items.explanation: Each Departmental Standing Committee has a strength of 31 members (21 from LS + 10 from RS).

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Who is the chairman of the Business Advisory Committee of Lok Sabha?
items.explanation: Speaker of Lok Sabha is the chairman of the Business Advisory Committee.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: What is the notice period required for a Public Member Bill?
items.explanation: 1 week prior notice should be given for a Public Member Bill.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Which parliamentary position automatically becomes the chairman of a committee of which he is a member (e.g., Committee on Private Members Bill)?
items.explanation: Deputy speaker automatically becomes the chairman of a committee of which he is a member.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Who brings a Private Bill in Parliament?
options: An MP who is not a minister
items.correctAnswer: An MP who is not a minister
items.explanation: A Private Bill is brought by an MP who is not a minister.
items.optionD: An MP who is not a minister

items.subject: Polity
items.question: What is the prior notice required for a Private Bill?
items.explanation: 1 Month Prior notice should be given for a Private Bill.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: In how many cases is a deadlock created for an ordinary bill?
items.explanation: A deadlock is created in three specific cases for an ordinary bill.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: What duration of time elapsing without bill passing by the other house creates a deadlock?
items.explanation: More than six months elapse from the date of reception without the bill being passed.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: From which country is the provision of Joint Sitting taken?
items.explanation: Provision of Joint sitting is taken from Australia.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Under Article 180, who acts as the Speaker when the office is vacant or the Speaker is absent?
items.explanation: The Deputy Speaker acts as the Speaker when office is vacant or absent.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Who decides on the disqualification of members under Article 192?
items.explanation: Disqualification decisions are made by the Governor along with the Election Commission of India.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: What is the penalty for sitting and voting before taking an oath or when disqualified under Article 193?
items.explanation: The penalty for sitting and voting when disqualified is a fine decided by the Legislature.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: In the case of an ordinary bill originating in the Legislative Council, what happens if the Legislative Assembly disagrees?
options: The bill lapses and there is no joint sitting provision in Part VI
items.correctAnswer: The bill lapses and there is no joint sitting provision in Part VI
items.explanation: If LA disagrees, the bill lapses with no provision for joint sitting in Part VI.
items.optionA: The bill lapses and there is no joint sitting provision in Part VI

items.subject: Polity
items.question: What is the maximum period the Legislative Council can delay an Ordinary Bill in total?
items.explanation: LC can only delay an Ordinary Bill by a maximum of 4 months total.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Within how many days must the Legislative Council return a Money Bill with or without recommendations?
items.explanation: The Legislative Council must return a Money Bill within 14 days.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Where can a Money Bill be introduced according to Article 198?
options: Only with President's prior approval in Parliament
items.explanation: A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Legislative Assembly.
items.optionC: Only with President's prior approval in Parliament

items.subject: Polity
items.question: What does Article 202 cover in the state legislative process?
items.explanation: Article 202 deals with the Annual Financial Statement, also known as the Budget.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Under Article 203, demands for grants can be made only on whose recommendation?
items.explanation: Demands for grants are made solely on the recommendation of the Governor.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: What power does Article 213 grant to the Governor during the recess of the legislature?
items.explanation: Article 213 grants the Governor power to promulgate Ordinances during legislative recess.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: What is the maximum total membership permitted for a Legislative Council according to Article 171?
items.explanation: Total members shall not exceed 1/3rd of Legislative Assembly with a minimum of 40 members.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Which Article prohibits courts from inquiring into legislative proceedings?
items.explanation: Article 212 specifies that courts shall not inquire into legislature proceedings.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: What category of members is nominated by the Governor to the Legislative Council under Article 171?
options: 1/6th members from literature, science, art, cooperative movement, social service
1/3rd members from literature, science, art, cooperative movement, social service
items.correctAnswer: 1/6th members from literature, science, art, cooperative movement, social service
items.explanation: 1/6th are nominated by the Governor from literature, science, art, cooperative movement, and social service.
items.optionB: 1/6th members from literature, science, art, cooperative movement, social service
items.optionD: 1/3rd members from literature, science, art, cooperative movement, social service

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Under Article 181, can the Speaker or Deputy Speaker preside during the consideration of a resolution for their own removal?
options: No, they are not to preside
Only if requested by the Governor
items.correctAnswer: No, they are not to preside
items.explanation: The Speaker or Deputy Speaker shall not preside during consideration of their own removal.
items.optionA: No, they are not to preside
items.optionC: Only if requested by the Governor

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Which Article deals with Bills Reserved for President's Consideration?
items.explanation: Article 201 deals with Bills Reserved for the President's Consideration.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: What is the subject matter of Articles 214 to 231?
items.explanation: Articles 214-231 cover the High Courts.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: According to Article 189, what kind of voting power does a presiding officer have in the first instance and in case of a tie?
options: Can vote in the first instance and also has a casting vote
Only a casting vote, no first instance vote
items.correctAnswer: Can vote in the first instance and also has a casting vote
items.explanation: The presiding officer can vote in the first instance and also has a casting vote.
items.optionA: Can vote in the first instance and also has a casting vote
items.optionB: Only a casting vote, no first instance vote

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Which constitutional amendment allowed for the appointment of the same person as the Governor of two or more states?
items.explanation: The 7th Constitutional Amendment allowed appointing the same person as Governor of two or more states.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: What is the minimum age requirement for appointment as Governor under Article 157?
items.explanation: A person must have completed 35 years of age to be appointed as Governor.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: Who appoints the Governor of a State?
items.explanation: Governor is appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: During whose pleasure does the Governor hold office?
items.explanation: Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: What fraction of the Legislative Council members are elected by graduates of 3 years or more?
items.explanation: 1/12th of total members are elected by graduates of 3 years or more.

items.subject: Polity
items.question: What is the normal term of office for a Governor from the date of assuming office?
items.explanation: Governor's term is 5 years from assuming office, subject to earlier removal or resignation.

items.subject: Polity

items.explanation: Schedule B of the 2nd IPR 1956 contained 12 industries for Public and Private Sectors.

items.subject: Economics
items.question: The 3rd IPR, 1977 was introduced by which government?
items.explanation: The 3rd IPR, 1977 was introduced by the Morarji Desai Government (Janata Party).

items.explanation: The Tiny Unit concept applied to small enterprises with investments below 1 lakh.

items.question: Who proposed the Gandhian Plan in 1944?
items.explanation: The Gandhian Plan of 1944 was formulated and proposed by S.N. Agarwal.

items.subject: Economics
items.question: What was the government control over industries through licensing called at its start?
items.explanation: Government control over industries through licensing was referred to as the start of License Raj.

items.question: The People's Plan of 1945 was formulated by whom?
items.explanation: The People's Plan was formulated by M.N. Roy based on Marxist Socialism.

items.explanation: M.N. Roy formed the Communist Party of India in Tashkent in 1920.

items.subject: Economics
items.question: Who formulated the Sarvodaya Plan in 1950?
items.explanation: The Sarvodaya Plan was formulated by Jayaprakash Narayan in 1950.

items.subject: Economics
items.question: What was the duration of India's First Five-Year Plan?
items.explanation: The duration of the First Five-Year Plan was from 1951 to 1956.

items.explanation: The First Five-Year Plan was based on the Harrod-Domar Model.
